newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. SUNY may have mishandled NCAA basketball cash.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. SUNY may have mishandled NCAA basketball cash.

text.p: A New York State watchdog on Monday said the State University College at Buffalo's athletic program might have misappropriated thousands of dollars that were collected at national basketball championships.

"My auditors identified many highly irregular transactions of cash collected during the National Collegiate Athletic Assocication basketball tournaments, which warrant further investigation, and as I recommended, State University at New York (SUNY) officials have referred these matter to the state attorney general," said H. Carl McCall, state comptroller, in prepared remarks.

The college's athletic director often kept tournament revenues in his personal account instead of depositing the money in an authorized SUNY account, failed to keep records to prove the funds were used for expenses that were allowed, and deposited cash in the wrong accounts, the auditors found.

At least $763,000 was collected from July 1992 to June 1995 from activities related to a three-day basketball tournament held by the NCAA for three years in a row, the college's Sports Complex, revenues from tickets for college athletic events, and private funds to support the athletic program.

Nearly $13,000 in cash and checks collected for the Sports Complex, which runs ice skating and rentals of the complex, and the Intercollegiate Atlhetic Account allegedly were used to pay for tournament expenses and other costs, the auditors said, adding the athletic director witheld over $17,000 of tournament funds that he said were used to pay expenses. Records to prove such payments were made were not maintained.
College auditors wrote the athletic director and told him $36,000 had been deposited to the wrong accounts, but there was no indication that SUNY followed up, McCall said.
Another problem surfaced over the accuracy of faculty attendance forms, and whether they fully account for leaves, a factor used to calculate retirement pay.

Buffalo State spent about $20.6 million in costs for faculty in 1994-95 and it collects about $3 million in cash from remote sites, McCall said, urging the SUNY administrators to improve controls at the Buffalo campus.
